headline: The RBI raised rates for the first time in nearly four years and foreign investors sold ₹6,121 crore of shares. The Nifty sits right on its support at 22,600, with a flat start expected.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: The dashboard's bias score is −28 (bearish), but only 2 of its 4 direction checks agree, because the options market is leaning the other way.

key_points.text: The RBI raised its main rate from 5.25% to **5.50%** and hinted at more. Costlier loans tend to slow profits and make shares less attractive.
Foreign investors (FIIs) sold **₹6,121 crore** of shares yesterday. Indian funds bought ₹4,597 crore, soaking up about three quarters of it.
The Nifty is below its 20, 50 and 200-day averages, with **lower highs and lower lows**: a downtrend.
Option traders bought bets on a rise at 23,000–23,200. This is the one signal that **disagrees** with the bearish picture.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: Price and futures data point down, but the options market is not convinced.

points.text: The data shows the Nifty at 22,603, **7% below** its 200-day average. Each bounce recently has stopped lower than the last.
Futures fell 0.76% while open futures contracts rose **1.8%**. Price down with more contracts usually means new bets on a fall.
Traders bought calls (bets on a rise) at 23,000–23,200 and sold puts at 22,400. My read: some expect a bounce, so the option step scores **+1.5**.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs bets on a rise) is a steady 0.89, and India VIX (expected swings) is 13.9, **mid-range**. Neither shows extreme fear or greed.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign investors are selling hard while Indian funds keep buying.

points.text: FIIs are **₹9,083 crore** net sellers this month. Reports link this to high US bond rates, a strong dollar and the RBI hike.
Indian funds (DIIs) bought ₹9,685 crore this month, slightly more. That is why the fall has been **slow, not sharp**.
FIIs hold only **9.2%** long in index futures, a huge bet against the market. Below 10% has often come before a fast buy-back rally, but there is no sign of one yet.
In September, FIIs sold most in financial companies (**₹13,147 crore**), oil and gas, and autos, per NSDL.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: High US rates, a strong dollar and costly oil all pull money away from India.

points.text: The US 10-year bond rate touched 5.37% yesterday, its **highest since 2002**. When safe US bonds pay this much, foreign money has less reason to buy Indian shares.
Fed minutes showed all officials backed September's hike, and US bill rates point to **another US hike**, likely by December.
The dollar is at a 1-year high and the rupee is near **96.8** per dollar, 2.4% weaker in a month. Brent crude is about 01, up 33% in 3 months.
US shares dipped only 0.2% from a record and gold fell 7.6% in a month. There is **no global panic**.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No big companies reported this week, but the results season starts tonight with TCS.

points.text: 16 results were filed in the last 7 days, **none from Nifty 50** companies, so they say little about the index.
TCS reports **today after market hours**. As the first big IT result, it sets the tone for IT stocks tomorrow.
HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank report on **17 Oct**. Banks are the Nifty's biggest part and what FIIs sold most.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: India inflation data and bank results in the next 10 days could confirm or break the downtrend.

points.text: India inflation data comes on **12 Oct at 4 pm**. A number above August's 4.82% would raise the chance of another RBI hike.
Weekly options expire on **13 Oct**, which can pull the index towards 22,600 or 23,000.
Proof the bearish read is wrong: FII long % jumping 3 points or more, and a close above **23,000**.
Worse news would be a close below **22,600**, more big FII selling, or US bond rates rising further.

levels.note: The Nifty closed just 3 points above the floor; a close below 22,600 would extend the downtrend, while a close above 23,000 would be the first sign of a real bounce.

watch.text: The open. GIFT Nifty was near 22,600 at 7:50 am, so a flat start right at the floor.
Fed official Waller speaks. Talk of more hikes could push US bond rates up.
US weekly jobless claims. A strong job market makes a US hike more likely.
TCS results after the close, call at 7 pm.

bottom_line: The dashboard leans bearish (score −28): price is in a downtrend, futures show new bets on a fall, and FIIs are heavily short and selling. Confidence is low, because only 2 of 4 checks agree and option traders are betting on a bounce from 22,600. Indian funds are cushioning the fall. The main risk to this read is a sudden rally if heavily short FIIs buy back quickly.
